chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud, from Sayf, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant is in a state of ease regarding his affairs, between him and forty years. So when he reaches forty years, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reveals to His two angels: "I have given this servant of Mine a lifespan, so be stringent and be strict, and be watchful, and record for him little of his deeds and much, and small and large."'

key_terms.فُسْحَةٍ: ease, spaciousness, or leeway in affairs
key_terms.قَلِيلَ عَمَلِهِ وَ كَثِيرَهُ: little of his deeds and much
key_terms.مَلَكَيْهِ: His two angels (typically Raqib and Atid)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's spiritual state and divine recording of deeds when they reach the age of forty?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual significance of the age of forty as a threshold where divine mercy transitions to stricter accountability. It reflects the scholarly view that the first four decades represent a period of grace and ease in worship, after which the recording angels (Kiraman Katibin) intensify their scrutiny of all deeds, signaling a mature phase of spiritual reckoning.

en.hubeali: H 14532 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Dawood, from Sayf, from Abu Baseer who said:

So when he reaches at the age of forty years, Allahazwj Reveals to Hisazwj two Angels: “Iazwj have Let Myazwj servant to get to this age, so stringent and be more strict with him and write down all from little, big, less, more from his deeds.
en.sarwar: 84. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Dawood, from Sayf, from Abu Baseer who said:

So when he reaches at the age of forty years, Allah (azwj) Reveals to His (azwj) two Angels: “I (azwj) have Let My (azwj) servant to get to this age, so stringent and be more strict with him and write down all from little, big, less, more from his deeds.
